notes.title: Running it Back to the Drawing Board
notes.content:
Hey All,

[h1][b]Blog[/b][/h1]

I'll leave this here as a spoiler for those that want to know what's being going in with the dev and the game.

Main Blog:
[expand type=showmore]
Let's get into it. Hi, I'm D, or Phaze if you prefer. I'm currently the only person working at OOMM Interactive. I have game dev friends and contractors who come in and help with different stuff if I don't specialize in it, but for the most part, the games don't happen if I'm not pushing them forward.

You may have heard about all the hubbub happening in the games and tech industry. It's a tough time in the tech sector and jobs are hard to come by. That's mostly what's been taking up my time the past few months, looking for work and then doing some dev for myself on the side.

As you might imagine, getting rejected, or not even getting replies from places, is tough on one's mental health. I'm lucky at least to have a place to stay, and savings to keep me going a while. I'm not going to go into depth of how I am, but sufficed to say, I'm trying new ways to dev, and diving into the deep end with this whole make a video game company thing.

Now on to the show!

I'm working on three games at the same time! Hahah......

Ok, a little background. I've been trying new things these past few months, and having multiple projects to switch between works best for me. Originally, I wanted to just stick to EEE and get it done, but that just sorta kept getting bogged down and bloated. I wanted it to just be done, as opposed to focusing on doing it well. A lot of avenues felt closed off, because it would take too long, and some tech debt related to the tech tree made the backend somewhat unstable.

That's all gonna change with the new multi project thing. If I don't feel up to working on something I can switch projects. This also has the benefits of letting ideas and design percolate longer, and possibly come up with better solutions.

I've currently finished up a game, Castaway Soul. It'll be coming out on the 5th of July, and I'll make a separate post for that. This one is actually fully finished before release. X)

I'll be working on a hyper-casual, sci-fi mobile game around bringing free wifi to the galaxy. The drones in that game actually informed how I could rework EEE to be a lot more fun. I'll also be working on a sequel to Castaway soul pretty much right after it releases.

As for EEE, it's still all in the planning stages. What's set for now (but still subject to change) is:
[list]
[*]There will be a "galaxy exploration" progress visible at all times;
[*]Self-replication will be moved to the new drones, drones will start out few and grow exponentially;
[*]Drones essentially can do almost all the work that previously went to buildings;
[*]Buildings are now more specialized, and can be demolished;
[*]All sites will have limited mineral resources, so they can be mined out;
[*]Energy will play a larger role, solar panels, solar sats, solar swarms will be more important than ever;
[*]Leaving a site will still save it's outputs, so old sites can still provide power and other resources, with there being a limit to the total number of sites before old ones start being abandoned;
[*]The Expedition Vessel will always be accessible, and data can be sent up without Ascending;
[*]The main focus will be on building space exploration drones, and observation stations to survey the galaxy faster;
[/list]
I think all these changes will make for a much more fun/engaging game, while adding that sort of griebly feel of drones clearing out the tiles bit by bit. This does mean that the game will take quite a bit longer to finish. Current aim is to have it done by this time next year

That's about it I think. If you got this far, thanks for taking the time to read all that (or at least skim it X) ). There's been a lot of positive feedback with the game, and it's been very encouraging. I want to finish this game, and I want to make it enjoyable for all those who stuck around. :)
[/expand]

[h3]TLDR:[/h3] Life's hard, stuff happens, and tends to keep happening. Getting back into working on the game, will be doing a top-down rebuild to base the game around drones, and will be bringing the main goal of the game more front and center.

notes.title: Updating to Build 7 - Rocketry
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

[h1][b]Blog[/b][/h1]
First off, I've decided to shift the focus back to be more tycoon.

There was a variety of elements from idle games that I was using just because they are expected of idle games, not because they work for the game. As such, a bunch of things have been changed around, chief among them being removal of Quanta. The speed controls are now just always available.

The next very big thing is an engine upgrade and implementation of ECS. The backend of the game has essentially been re-written. I'll be moving forward with more optimizations in further updates, there's still more stuff that can be turned to ECS to better performance gains.

The newly added mechanics are the orbital layer, and with it launch pads and satellites. These provide boosts to all sites on the same planet, giving a longer term investment. With that comes the new Tier One tech tree, which has harder to get data, but powerful upgrades around the orbital layer.

[b]TL;DR: Game has been shifted back more towards tycoon, with elements and design in place for those that want a more idle experience. Orbital layer, rockets and sats are in. There is a Large amount of backend changes in this build, so please post on steam discussions or our discord if you find any bugs, or issues/systems that might've been missed or badly balanced.

[u]If you are on the experimental branch, switch back to default to get the newest version.[/u][/b]

[previewyoutube=IDmXmyIrroU;full][/previewyoutube]

Now, on to the main show:
[b](Hard Reset is Recommended due to backend changes)[/b]

[h1][b]New Features[/b][/h1]
[list]
[*] Upgraded to Unity 2022.3 and ECS
[*] ECS implementation gives Major performance gains
[*] Added Orbital Layer, Launch Pads, and Satellites
[*] Added a new Tier One Tech tree, and a new type of Data
[*] Added Warping to Other Planets
[*] Vessel Modules, ship upgrades that move with you from planet to planet
[*] Added Way more tutorials to help explain game mechanics as they come up
[*] Added multi-build setting and more mouse controls
[*] Data novelty mechanic
[/list]

[h2][b]Changes[/b][/h2]
[list]
[*] Field Station:
- Reduced cost and cost creep
- No longer produces data, just researches tiles
- Researched tiles are needed for the new data type
- No longer has infinite range, only researches adjacent tiles
[*] Survey Hub:
- Charge limit is now dependent on distance to nearest unexplored tile
- This means the survey hub will charge slower the further it gets from unexplored tiles
- Added a new tech to make cooldown be divided by number of volatiles processors on site
- Rebalanced charge and cooldown for the above changes
- Survey Hubs should be faster overall, but too significantly reduced if left idle
[*] Changed the build menu to use icons instead of building names
- Building names will show up at the bottom of the menu when a building is selected
[*] Changes to Tech Tree:
- The tech tree now uses tooltips for easier readability as all zoom levels
- The tech tree now has colors to indicate if a node can be researched, and if there is enough data available to research it
[/list]


[h2][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed clusters being able to overlap
[*] Fixed clusters sometimes highlighting incorrect tiles
[*] Fixed cluster borders not properly recoloring for adjacency
[*] Backend changes fixed a number of issues
[*] A number of small fixes that I forgot to write down to put here X)
[/list]

notes.title: Updating to Build 6
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

[h1][b]Blog[/b][/h1]
Change of plans from what was planned for this build. The next prestige layer was taking longer than expected, currently at about 10 pages of design, with several different iterations designed, redesigned, and discarded. With that in mind, the next prestige layer will be released bit by bit, as opposed to trying to make the entire thing and once, and taking a month or more.

Didn't want to leave it that long without an update, especially with update 5 leaving the game as more of an active tycoon game, as opposed to an idle game.

And so, I present the idle gameplay overhaul of build 6. Most of the game has been rebalanced to allow for actual idle gameplay, with map sizes on average being 10 times larger before running into the impassable terrain soft lock. The self-replication has been moved up so it's available sooner, and survey hubs now behave more like the landing ship exploration. Most of the tech costs are now more expensive, but with these changes, the game can just be left to it's own devices for a few hours after the initial expedition site setup.

There were also issues of players not being shown where to go, or how to ascent, so a new Getting Started screen has been added to hopefully help with that.

[b]TL;DR: Game is now more idle as opposed to idle/tycoon, orbital layer is being worked on. There is a Large amount of changes in this build, so please post on steam discussions or our discord if you find any bugs, or issues/systems that might've been missed or badly balanced[/b]

Now, on to the main show:

[h1][b]New Features[/b][/h1]
[list]
[*] Added a Getting Started screen to guide new players through the start of the game
[*] Added a Building Management menu, allows for global production and expansion control, and has a new toggle once expansion is researched to set whether expansion is on or off by default on build.
[*] Added Tooltips to most buttons and number displays
[*] Added a hard reset option to the settings menu
[/list]

[h2][b]Changes[/b][/h2]
[list]
[*] Map sizes are now 10 times larger before running into blocker soft lock
[*] All building charge timers have been reduced by 50%
[*] Matter Extractor:
- now produces (M) 0.1, for (E) 0.1 | down from (M) 1 and (E) 1
[*] Solar Collector:
- now produces (E) 0.1 | down from (E) 1
[*] Volatiles Processor:
- now produces (V) 0.1, for (M) 0.2 and (E) 0.2 | down from (V) 1, for (M) 1 and (E) 1
[*] Survey Hubs:
- higher initial build cost
- unlimited range
- randomly explores tiles
- expends (V) 0.4 | down from (V) 1
[*] Field Stations:
- research tiles more slowly
- they consume (MEV) 0.1 more, and produce (D) 0.0001 per cycle, per researched tile on the map
[*] Cluster buildings:
- give a modifier to their building type, accelerating their self-replication speed
- add +0.1 to datalith value on Ascent, for the same building type | down from +1 datalith value
[*] Survey Hub Clusters now accelerate all exploration speed.
[*] Landing Ship description now refers to the survey drone tech, until that tech is researched
[*] Autosave is now done every 30s
[*] Mountain blocker:
- now starts with a 0.01% chance, but creeps faster
- limited at 95% max
[*] Canyon blocker:
- now starts at 10% chance, but creeps very slowly
- limited to 90% max
[*] Cost creep is now limited to base cost * 1 million
[*] Flavor/lore change, buildings now move out from the landing ship if no fib pods are available for orbital drop.
[/list]


[h2][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed Field Station not properly updating charge and cooldown limit
[*] Fixed progress bar not showing on buildings with a stored charge on load
[*] Fixed spelling on adjacency tech
[*] Fixed the UI windows not properly hiding on some resolutions
[*] Changed how the windows animate to make them more responsive
[*] A number of small fixes that I forgot to write down to put here X)
[/list]

notes.title: Updating to Build 5
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

[h1][b]Blog[/b][/h1]
Bit of a late update this week, had some IRL issues that got in the way.

This week, two new systems have been added: Adjacency, and Clustering.
Adjacency needs to be researched, and will have you putting more thought into where to land your buildings. Clustering works on top of that, if a building has the same type all around it, a new create cluster button will appear, allowing them to merge. These clusters provide Large buffs to their production and also increase amount of dataliths gained from that type of building on Ascent.

I've decided to hold off on the Codex system. It's basically a wiki and tutorial system, and kinda boring to work on. So instead of one large push, I'll just be adding bits and pieces as I work on other things.

[b]For the next update[/b], it's going to be a bigger one. The plan is to add the next prestige layer, and that will bring new game mechanics as well. That being said, it will probably take more than a week, mostly likely a few weeks. If you'd like to get updates on the progress, they will be posted on our discord.

A lot of people have been asking for where they can join the community or donate to support the game, so going forward, we'll be including links at the bottom of these update posts.

Lastly, I'm going to take the rest of the week off, just to recharge from IRL stuff, and then get right back into it.

Now, on to the main show:

[h1][b]New Features[/b][/h1]
[list]
[*] Added Adjacency
[*] Added Clustering
[*] Added new techs to enable and boost various building adjacency
[*] Added a new Early Access Screen
[*] Added a new End of Content Screen
[/list]

[h2][b]Changes[/b][/h2]
[list]
[*] Survey Hubs now should Max Exploration Range in their supplemental Description
[*] Buildings that can expand now automatically turn off expansion if there are no available free tiles around them
[/list]


[h2][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed researched tiles not saving and not counting for Ascent
[*] Fixed the Mountain and Canyon chance creep reduction tech making the cost creep actually decrease over time, leading to way larger maps than planned.
[*] Fixed Field Station Production and Building Cost being swapped
[*] Optimized orbital and research tree objects
[*] A variety of other tweaks and issues that are too small or too interconnected to mention here

notes.title: Updating to Build 2
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

[h1][b]Blog[/b][/h1]
It's been one week since we release Eclectic Expansion Enterprise, and it's been a ride. As a solo dev, it's been great to see people engaging with and enjoying something I've created. This is just the beginning, and there's plenty planned for the road ahead!

That being said, this was my first time releasing to multiple platforms at the same time, and switching between the WebGL and PC build caused some unexpected issues. I think I've dealt with a large number of those bugs, so this build should be much more stable. Keep those bug reports coming though, I want to make sure there's as few bugs in the game as possible.

Now, on to the main show:

[h1][b]New Features[/b][/h1]
[list]
[*] Added an offline progression mechanic
[*] Added cost scaling to all buildings
[*] Buildings now have a hollow image when turned off
[*] Added a tech node to unlock the Field Station
[*] Added a tech node to for Volatiles Processor self-replication
[*] Added a large number of new tech nodes
[*] Added a new setting menu for changing resolution and window setting
[*] Added a new setting menu to control animation speed
[/list]

[h2][b]Changes[/b][/h2]
[list]
[*] Halved cost of most Matter Extractor and Solar Collector techs
[*] Changed the dataliths per income to instead use number of buildings(no need to turn off things before Ascent anymore!)
[/list]


[h2][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed Matter Extractor and Solar Collector not self-replicating properly
[*] Fixed Landing Ship charge and cooldown increments being 0
[*] Fixed Solar Collector Optimization Mk II not saving properly
[*] Fixed Survey Hub not reducing it's volatiles expenditure when at max explore range
[*] Fixed buildings not powering off properly from the building details menu
[*] Fixed an ordering issue causing survey hubs to create extra tiles on load (if loading a map that has survey hubs on it, some buildings might shift around. New sites and future saves will not have this issue)
[*] A variety of other tweaks and issues that are too small or too interconnected to mention here
[/list]
